sentences.text: Revenue grew from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025, a 34.8% compound annual rate [F1][F10][F196].
The steepest move was FY2017, when revenue rose 104.0% as the number of advertisements delivered increased [D36][P81].

Operating loss nearly doubled from $702.1 million in FY2021 [F16] to $1,395.3 million in FY2022 [F17]; the filing attributes lower Adjusted EBITDA to higher cost of revenue and operating expenses [P42].
FY2025 operating margin improved 5.7pp to -9.0%, the best in the window [D419][F30][D554].
In FY2025 advertising revenue of $5.19 billion added 5.3pp to growth [S39][D538], and other revenue of $745 million added 5.4pp [S42][D545].
Advertising impressions rose about 17% while cost per impression fell about 10%, and other revenue grew on subscriber numbers [P24].
Advertising growth slowed to 5.8% [D537] from 11.2% [D534], while other revenue reached 12.6% of revenue [D543].
Operating costs grew 5.1% [D423] against 10.6% revenue growth [D406], lifting incremental operating margin to 44.8% [D429].
Loss per share narrowed 35.7% [D409] against a 34.0% fall in net loss [D408], with diluted shares up 2.1% [D425].
Operating margin of -9.0% [F30][D554] is the window high, against a median of -32.4% [D555] and a low of -422.5% [D553].
The 5.7pp FY2025 gain [D419] came from cost of revenue (1.1pp [D431]), R&D (1.3pp [D432]) and other operating lines (3.3pp [D433]).
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on lower advertising spend and prior-year event timing [P22], while R&D rose $101.9 million on product investment [P23].
The passages provided do not explain the 7.9% cost-of-revenue rise [D421] behind the 1.1pp gain [D431].
Net margin of -7.8% [F50] sits 1.2pp above operating margin [F30], partly because other income of $68.9 million [X130] included $96.7 million of extinguishment gains [P18].
Operating cash flow of $656 million [F80] and free cash flow of $437 million [F100] compare with a net loss of $460.5 million [F40].
The gap is mainly non-cash: operating cash flow starts from the loss and adds back $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation [P13][X90] and $164 million of D&A [P13][X80].
Free cash flow margin of 7.4% [D393] is the window high [D560], against a window median of -4.1% [D561]; capex was 3.7% of revenue [D392].
Net cash fell from $197 million in FY2022 [D256] to net debt of $596 million [D399], a sustained decline [R3].
Net debt equals 10.1% of revenue [D400], ranking at the 0th percentile of the five-company internet peer group [D578], against a peer median net cash of 45.0% of revenue [D579].
Interest expense rose to $122 million from $21.6 million [X100][X99], primarily from the 2033 and 2034 notes issued in 2025 [P19].
Buybacks of $751 million [X156] were 171.7% of free cash flow [D402], so repurchases are not funded by cash generation.
High severity and persistent: a net loss in each of ten years [R1]; FY2025's $460.5 million loss [F40] was 34.0% smaller than FY2024's $698 million [D408][F39].
High and ongoing: stock-based compensation of $1.02 billion [X90] was 17.1% of revenue [D390] and 191.1% of the operating loss [D404], above 10% for nine years [R2].
Medium, three years: buybacks were 171.7% of FY2025 free cash flow [R4][D402] and 142.3% in FY2024 [D354]; the passages provided do not explain the FY2025 repurchase amount.
Added flag: advertising growth slowed to 5.8% [D537] as cost per impression fell about 10% [P24], so pricing is now weighing on growth.
Advertising growth returning above 11.2% [D534] would confirm a recovery; growth below 5.8% [D537] would reverse the trend, as shown in the FY2026 10-K.
Repurchases below free cash flow of $437 million [F100], against 171.7% of it in FY2025 [D402], would show buybacks paced to cash generation in the next 10-K.
Operating margin below -9.0% [F30][D554] would reverse the FY2025 improvement in the FY2026 10-K.
